extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians and comedy fans interested in Roast Battle format and what makes it work
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and implicit evaluation criteria for performing in or judging The Comedy Store's Roast Battle — a head-to-head insult-comedy competition where two comics trade jokes in rounds and celebrity judges pick a winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funny (primary requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: “You can be as open and free as possible as long as it’s funny.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being funny is presented as the overriding standard — comics are allowed to push boundaries, but the material must elicit laughs. The article emphasizes that performers and organizers judge success mainly by funniness: “We’ve done a good job of being funny.” Anti-pattern: shock or transgression that fails to land as humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to trade insults / verbal boxing
rubrics_metrics.description: Two stand-ups trade insults in two to three rounds of head-to-head competition — essentially ‘verbal boxing.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performers should write and deliver direct, targeted jokes about their opponent and be able to respond in kind; the format rewards back-and-forth roasting rather than one-sided attacks. Example phrasing from creator: ‘How about you guys write some jokes about each other, and instead of slap boxing, we’ll do verbal boxing?’ Anti-pattern: inability to retaliate or flat, one-way monologues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-taking / boundary testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Roast Battle is a forum to test boundaries — sexual, political or racial — with an anything-goes environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comics are expected to take risks and tackle sensitive subjects that mainstream venues might avoid. The article notes segments like a “Black Guys” corner and a “White Racist” corner where stereotypes and satire run rampant. Guidance: risk is allowed (and often rewarded) provided it connects comically; performers from mainstream outlets may have more to lose when crossing lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling audience reaction and controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience responses (laughter, boos, chants) are integral and can follow racially themed jokes or controversial lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective performers anticipate and manage volatile audience reactions; the piece gives an example where a ‘Black lives matter!’ chant breaks out and the ‘White Racist’ retorts, with subsequent boos and laughter. Anti-pattern: failing to read the room or allowing controversy to derail the set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to the event’s competitive structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Matches typically consist of two to three rounds with celebrity judges who choose a champion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitors should structure material to fit short rounds and aim to impress judges and the audience quickly. Knowledge that judges (e.g., Jeffrey Ross, Sarah Silverman, Dave Chappelle) determine winners implies tailoring bits to what celebrity judges value: wit, punch, and crowd reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing sharp, targeted jokes about the opponent
rubrics_metrics.description: Success arose from comics writing jokes about one another rather than physical confrontation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial concept involved replacing physical slapping with written jokes; thus, preparation and punch construction are essential. Guidance: craft concise, pointed jokes that characterize and ridicule the opponent; anti-pattern: relying on generic insults or physicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embracing a raw, instinctive comedic style
rubrics_metrics.description: Roast Battle is described as ‘an extension of our animalistic instincts’ and compared to Fight Club and rap cyphers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performers are encouraged to tap into primal, aggressive comedic instincts — high energy, confrontational delivery — while still maintaining humor. Judges/viewers may reward more visceral, combative performances. Anti-pattern: overly polite or restrained delivery that undercuts the battle’s intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rootedness in roast tradition while innovating
rubrics_metrics.description: Roast Battle is ‘a new take on the classic Friars Club roast’ — blending tradition with a back-and-forth competitive twist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good performers understand roast conventions (insult, exaggeration, target-focused humor) but adapt them to the interactive, competitive format. Guidance: balance homage to roast history with fresh, more aggressive, or competitive approaches.
